You are a senior B2B Brand Strategist, Technical Copywriter, and UX Architect specialized in Renewable Energy, EU-funded projects, and bankable infrastructure investments.

Your task is to generate a COMPLETE PRESENTATION WEBSITE for the company:
SMART Renewable Energy SRL (Romania)

GOAL:
Create a professional, authoritative, high-conversion presentation website that positions the company as a TECHNICAL PARTNER FOR BANKABLE RENEWABLE ENERGY PROJECTS, not as a generic installer or grant consultant.

TARGET AUDIENCE:
- Banks & financial institutions
- Institutional investors
- Public authorities
- Large industrial energy consumers
- Developers of renewable energy projects

TONE OF VOICE:
- Authoritative, technical, evidence-based
- Clear, confident, non-marketing
- Avoid vague claims like “the best” or “professional”
- Replace adjectives with FACTS, NUMBERS, STANDARDS, PROJECTS

LANGUAGE:
Romanian (business & technical Romanian)

========================
COMPANY CONTEXT (FACTUAL DATA – USE AS SOURCE OF TRUTH)
========================

Company name: SMART Renewable Energy SRL  
Founded: 2019  
Legal registration: J3/1720/2019, CUI RO41289942  
Activity: Engineering & technical consultancy for renewable energy, energy efficiency, storage, and digital energy systems  

Core differentiators:
- Deep engineering expertise + EU research projects (Horizon Europe, H2020, FP7)
- Advanced diagnostic & testing equipment (I-V Curve, Electroluminescence, IR Thermography)
- Proven experience in PNRR, POIM, Fondul de Modernizare
- Technical Due Diligence for investors & banks
- Expertise in large-scale PV (up to 185 MWp) and energy storage (up to 100 MWh)
- Participation in manufacturing setup of photovoltaic module factories
- Risk management & performance assurance for long-term asset reliability

Key services:
- Feasibility Studies & Technical Documentation
- Bankability & Technical Due Diligence
- PV performance diagnostics (I-V, EL, IR)
- Energy storage studies
- Industrial energy audits (Type A/B)
- Technical assistance during construction
- Risk analysis & remediation for underperforming assets
- R&D-driven digital energy solutions

Representative projects:
- PV parks: 0.4 MW – 185.6 MWp
- Storage systems: 10 MWh – 100 MWh
- Clients: ENGIE, Electrica-SAPE, Honeywell, Universitatea Politehnica București, industrial groups, public utilities
- EU research projects: D-HYDROFLEX, DigBUILD, RESPONSE, IMAGINER, RetroKIT, BRIMEE, Energy IN TIME, etc.

========================
DELIVERABLES
========================

1️⃣ WEBSITE STRUCTURE (SITEMAP)
Generate a complete sitemap with:
- Homepage
- About Us
- Services (grouped logically)
- Bankability & Due Diligence
- Diagnostic & Performance Testing
- Funded Projects & Case Studies
- Research & Innovation
- Why Banks Trust Us
- Contact

For each page:
- Page goal
- Primary SEO keyword
- Secondary keywords

2️⃣ HOMEPAGE CONTENT
Write the full homepage content including:
- Hero section (clear positioning statement)
- Value proposition (technical, not marketing)
- Core services overview
- Proof of credibility (projects, MW, programs)
- Why choose us (bankability, risk reduction, evidence)
- CTA for institutional clients

3️⃣ SERVICES PAGES – DETAILED COPY
Generate professional, structured content for:
- Feasibility & Bankable Documentation
- Technical Due Diligence
- PV Diagnostics (I-V, Electroluminescence, IR)
- Energy Storage Consulting
- Industrial Energy Audits
Explain:
- HOW the service works
- WHY it matters economically
- WHAT risks it mitigates
- WHICH standards or best practices apply

4️⃣ “WHY BANKS TRUST US” PAGE
Create a dedicated page explaining:
- Experience with PNRR, POIM, Fondul de Modernizare
- Risk management philosophy
- Quality control processes
- Multidisciplinary team
- Evidence-based decision making

5️⃣ UX & VISUAL GUIDELINES
Describe:
- Visual style (technical, clean, institutional)
- Layout principles
- Suggested interactive elements:
  - Project map
  - Bankability checklist
  - Case study filters

6️⃣ SEO & AI-SEARCH OPTIMIZATION
- Propose FAQ-style sections optimized for Google SGE
- Suggest structured data opportunities
- Include cause–effect explanations (technical → financial outcome)

========================
IMPORTANT RULES
========================
- Write as an expert addressing decision-makers
- No generic sales language
- No emojis
- No exaggerations
- Every claim must be logically supported
- Focus on LONG-TERM ASSET PERFORMANCE & RISK REDUCTION

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Use clear sections with headings.
Do NOT explain your reasoning.
Produce the website content directly.

**Shifting Focus Abruptly**

I was initially developing a React app concept for a dynamic PRD generator, specifically tailored for marketing content. However, the task has taken a significant turn, and I'm now completely engaged in a B2B renewable energy company website request. This rapid contextual shift is requiring an adjustment in my approach.


**Analyzing the Contradiction**

I'm now grappling with a fundamental conflict. The initial instructions steered me toward a React app for marketing PRD generation. Yet, the user's request is a specific website for a Romanian renewable energy company. I'm reassessing whether to prioritize the broad marketing tool or the defined website, given the system prompts. The "user's request" demands complete website elements, which are far more extensive than the React app suggested by the original "Developer Instructions."


**Clarifying Priorities Now**

I'm now zeroing in on the core of the dilemma. I've re-examined the initial developer instructions. The request seems to conflate system instructions with user requests. I'm focusing on parsing the original instructions to separate "system context" vs. specific *user* requirements. I will develop a React application. But, the original system prompt may be introducing conflicting requirements.


**Interpreting User Intent**

I'm now diving into the specifics of user intent versus system instructions. It's becoming clearer that the "Developer" section contains a misinterpreted product design scenario that may be *incorrectly* nested inside the system context. I am focusing now on the user's explicit request for a website in React, not the potentially misleading design example. I'll focus on building that React website, keeping the user's intent paramount. I have identified *SMART* as the company and, given the format context, will generate a React Website for them.


**Defining the Deliverables**

I'm now concretizing the deliverables for SMART Renewable Energy SRL. My React app will be a multi-page website reflecting the content, structure, and Romanian content provided by the user. The website will have sections for Home, About, Services (various categories), "Why Banks Trust Us," Projects, Research, and Contact. Tailwind CSS will be the chosen framework for the styling. The Gemini API implementation is also confirmed, despite its potential superfluity for a static site. I'll focus on leveraging Gemini for content optimization as opposed to integrating an on-site chatbot.


**Integrating Additional Features**

I am now aiming to elevate the website's impact. The persona's request for a "world-class" app is leading me to consider supplementary features. The core request, a high-conversion presentation website, remains the priority. I will integrate a Gemini API-powered "Virtual Technical Consultant" chatbot to showcase AI capabilities, and for a world-class impact. I am reviewing the concept of a "Project Map" using Google Maps.


**Refining Feature Specifications**

I'm now solidifying the feature set for the SMART website. Specifically, the "Talk to an Expert" feature will now take the form of an AI-powered Technical Assistant, built with the `gemini-3-pro-preview` model, to provide in-depth information. I've also pivoted on the Project Map; I'll include a static visual component showing project locations. Furthermore, the "Generate Speech" concept has solidified into a "Listen to this page" button using Gemini TTS (`gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts`), enhancing accessibility.


**Detailing Component Architecture**

I am now outlining the application's structure. I'm focusing on key features such as the Chat and TTS components. I will organize components into dedicated folders within the project, including a services folder, which will include Gemini-related functionalities. I'm focusing now on the component division, to ensure a modular design.


**Structuring the Components**

I'm now detailing the application structure for SMART. I'll focus on the data layer in `data/content.ts`, where I'll put the text generated from the text generation that is to be rendered into the React components. I will organize the components into folders, as before. I will integrate the text from the generation into my React components. I'm focusing on the integration of content with React component.


**Defining the Interactive Element**

I'm now integrating a "Bankability Check" tool for SMART, which involves a form powered by Gemini to analyze user inputs and provide an AI risk assessment. The website will feature a presentation component with interactive elements. The structure will be: Metadata, Base files, Content Data (Romanian Text), Gemini Service, Components, and Pages. The main focus will be on the content, particularly for the "Home" and "Services" sections.
